GraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale: The reference review (mark-private research/2026-10-20-multi-source-workspace-references.md) established that the multi-root substrate already exists and the work is routing/UX consistency. The dispatcher shape follows the review's gate 3 verbatim: one open-mode API, everything routes through it, distinct origins for telemetry-grade logging. The chooser-default rule (Add preselected) follows the owner decision that ambiguous inputs must offer the same two operations everywhere with the safe non-destructive default. Menu vocabulary adopts the explicit Add Folder… / Replace Workspace… pair from VS Code/Zed while deferring their multi-window and workspace-file features per the owner's scope boundary. iCloud "correct linking" was researched 2026-10-22 (backlog addendum): iCloud Drive is an ordinary folder tree the standard picker already offers; `mt_pick_folder` already persists a security-scoped bookmark (m047) so App-Store builds re-access the root across relaunches; FSEvents watchers already observe materialization of remote changes. The only iCloud-specific v1 work is hygiene (dot-entry parity keeps `.icloud` placeholders out of the tree) and honest failure copy for evicted/offline reads; triggering downloads is deferred because it needs an objc bridge (`startDownloadingUbiquitousItem`) or `brctl` subprocess and its own progress UX, none of which the reported use case requires to start benefiting from multi-root.

Alternatives.Alternative: Keep one "Open Folder…" command and make it always add (status quo plus nothing): rejected — the owner-approved experience names explicit Add and Replace, and replace-by-drop/clipboard with add-by-menu is exactly the inconsistent routing this change removes.

Route folder drop/clipboard directly to Add (never replace) and drop the chooser: rejected — replacing is a real user intent the concept preserves, and silently either adding or replacing was the original complaint surface; one chooser with a safe default keeps both intents explicit.

Close all tabs on Replace (VS Code "open folder" semantics) including standalone files: rejected as too destructive — tabs not under removed roots keep their files untouched; Replace resets the workspace roots, not the whole window.
Per-root metadata chips / workspace switcher UI: rejected for v1 — no owner request; the folder-switcher header and Open Recent already cover switching.

iCloud deep integration (download triggers, NSMetadataQuery, ubiquitous-item badges): rejected for v1 — the happy path needs none of it; placeholder hiding plus failure notices deliver the use case without new platform API surface. Recorded as a follow-up candidate in the backlog addendum.
Security-scoped bookmark work: none needed — m047 already bookmarks every folder pick and rescues reads; this change only covers it with synthetic-path tests (review gate 8).

DeferredDecisions.Decision: Accelerator for "Replace Workspace…": none in v1 (palette + menu only). If users ask, CmdOrCtrl+Alt+Shift+O is the natural candidate; must pass the existing key-collision checks first.
Whether the restore-degradation notice should also offer a "Remove from Recent" action on the missing root: deferred until the notice exists and real usage shows the need.

Whether duplicate-filename tab suffixes should use parent-directory names instead of owning-root names when the file sits outside every root: implementation may use parent directory for rootless tabs; exact presentation is a UX review point in the four-corner pass.
Download-triggering UX for evicted iCloud files (needs-download rows, progress, offline copy): follow-up change; v1 contract is hide placeholders + non-silent read failure.

Scenarios.Scenario: Dmitry's original case: an iCloud "Notes" root (picked from the picker's iCloud Drive sidebar) open beside a local repo root; both render as separate collapsible sections; search for a phrase returns hits from both with `Notes/…` and `repo/…` owner labels; relaunch restores both roots in order.

Drop a second folder onto the window with one root open: chooser appears with Add preselected; Add appends the root; choosing Replace warns because a dirty tab lives under the current root; Cancel leaves everything untouched.

"Optimize Mac Storage" evicts a synced file mid-session: the tree loses the file (remove event) and never shows the `.Name.md.icloud` placeholder; opening the still-listed file before eviction completes surfaces a read-failure notice, not silence.

App-Store build relaunch with an iCloud root: the persisted bookmark re-grants access (existing m047 path); if iCloud is signed out, the root is skipped with a visible notice and the other roots, tabs and the active tab still restore.
